summary: In this story, a boy on a desert camping trip loses his compass and must find his way back to camp before dark using landmarks and the stars.
introduce: Show the title “The Lost Compass” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: to find your way from one place to another
the way something points or the way you need to go
a sudden strong feeling of fear that makes it hard to think

challengeTerms.def: to figure out your direction or position compared to your surroundings
a group of stars that forms a pattern in the night sky
confused about which direction you are facing or where you are

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that if you get lost, the smartest thing to do is keep walking in any direction? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how Fahad used both calm thinking and knowledge of landmarks and stars to find his way back to camp.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review navigate, direction, and panic, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses orient, constellation, and disoriented to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
